title: StatusPageView
wrapsNative: List with Section headers (or a ScrollView with a VStack), NavigationLink to an incident's detail, refreshable(action:) for a new check, and a Form-style field and button for subscribing
summary: A recipe, not a component: a service status page as an in-app screen, with the overall state, active incidents and their updates, each service's state and uptime history, and an email subscription.
whenToUse: When an app shows the health of its own or a customer's services: an in-app status screen, the status tab of a monitoring product, or a support screen during an outage.
whenNotToUse: For one service's history alone use MonarchUptimeBar; for one incident's updates use MonarchIncidentTimeline; for a short outage notice above other content use MonarchCalloutBanner with placement .page. A public status website stays on the web.
api: List { Section { MonarchCalloutBanner(overallTitle, message: updated, tone: overallTone) } Section("Active incidents") { ForEach(incidents) { NavigationLink { ScrollView { MonarchIncidentTimeline(incident.updates) } } label: { Text(title); MonarchStatusBadge(state, size: .sm) } } } Section("Services") { ForEach(services) { Text(name); MonarchStatusBadge(state, size: .sm); MonarchUptimeBar(name, segments: days, size: .sm) } } Section("Subscribe to updates") { MonarchTextField("Email", text: $email); MonarchButton("Subscribe", variant: .primary) { … } } }.refreshable { await reload() }

states.name: operational
states.description: The banner reads "All systems operational" in the success tone.

states.name: degraded or partial outage
states.description: The banner takes the warning tone and the worst service state; affected services show their badge.

states.name: maintenance
states.description: "Under maintenance" in the info tone; scheduled work is listed as an incident with the maintenance stage.

states.name: no data
states.description: "Awaiting first checks" in the neutral tone; uptime bars show no-data segments.

states.name: subscribing
states.description: The Subscribe button shows progress; the result replaces the field's helper text.

appearance: System list sections on the grouped background. The overall state is a MonarchCalloutBanner, states are MonarchStatusBadge words with tone and icon, history is MonarchUptimeBar segments in the status roles, and updates are a MonarchIncidentTimeline. All follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ships StatusPageView as one component with a header, stats row, legend, maintenance list, past incidents grouped by day and a subscribe form. On iOS it is a recipe of existing components in a List: the stats row and legend are left out (each MonarchUptimeBar can show its legend and reads its own summary), an incident opens its timeline in a detail screen instead of expanding in place, and pull to refresh replaces the web's polling. The web's deriveOverallState is a short function in the recipe (worst of down, partial, degraded, maintenance, operational). Android plans it as a recipe as well.
accessibility: Section titles are headers, so the rotor moves between incidents, services and subscribing.
The overall state is the banner's title read with its tone name; service states are badge words, not only colours.
Each MonarchUptimeBar reads a summary of the period and is adjustable day by day.
The incident timeline reads each update with its stage, time and author.
The subscribe result is the field's helper text; post an announcement when it changes so VoiceOver hears it.
edgeCases: With no services, show MonarchEmptyState in the services section instead of an empty list.
With many services, group them in one Section per service group.
Incident times use MonarchIncidentTimeline's time zone (UTC by default); pass the page's time zone when it has one.
Long service names wrap above the badge at the largest text sizes.
